author: sungeunk
title: Smart CI fails with SSL certificate verify failed self-signed certificate
key_errors: ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: self-signed certificate (_ssl.c:1000)
urllib.error.URLError: <urlopen error [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: self-signed certificate (_ssl.c:1000)>
root_cause: Smart CI script (smart_ci.py) failed while calling GitHub API via ghapi/fastcore to compare commits for the merge-queue target branch. The runner's SSL context encountered a self-signed certificate during the HTTPS handshake with api.github.com, causing an immediate SSLCertVerificationError. This is a transient infrastructure/network issue where an intermediate proxy or corporate certificate is intercepting TLS traffic, resulting in a certificate chain that Python's ssl module cannot verify.
reproduction_steps: Not reproducible locally outside CI. The failure is runner/network-environment specific.
recommended_actions: Re-add the PR to the merge queue - the failure is transient (network/SSL infrastructure issue).
If the issue recurs frequently, investigate whether a corporate TLS intercepting proxy is misconfigured on the runner pool.
Consider adding SSL verification retry logic or certificate bundle override in smart_ci.py for resilience.
prevention_strategies: Monitor runner SSL certificate chain configuration. If a MITM/proxy certificate is expected, install it in the system CA bundle used by Python.
historical_context: No prior occurrences of this specific SSL self-signed certificate failure in the pattern database. Other Network-category failures have been seen (ECONNREFUSED, ENOTFOUND, etc.).
